input-size-and-operation-counts.title: Count the pair checks
input-size-and-operation-counts.prompt: Watch a nested scan of four items. The outer index moves once per item. The inner index only looks to the right.

frames.label: Start
frames.narration: Nothing has been compared. n is 4.

frames.label: Outer 0
frames.narration: Index 0 pairs with the three items to its right.

frames.label: Outer 1
frames.narration: Index 1 pairs with two items to its right. The total is 5.

frames.label: Outer 2
frames.narration: Index 2 pairs with one item. The total is 6, which is 4 * 3 / 2.

asymptotic-growth.title: Compare growth
asymptotic-growth.prompt: The same n is plugged into three formulas. Read which one pulls away.

frames.label: n = 4
frames.narration: Linear is still the smallest, but the three are close.

frames.label: n = 16
frames.narration: n² is already 256. n log2 n is 64.

frames.label: n = 1024
frames.narration: The quadratic count is about a million. The linear count is still 1024.

loop-invariants.title: Insert 1 into a sorted prefix
loop-invariants.prompt: The prefix to the left of the active item stays sorted. Watch the hole move.

frames.label: Before insert
frames.narration: The prefix [3] is sorted. 1 is the next key.

frames.label: Shift
frames.narration: 3 moves right because it is greater than 1. The hole is at index 0.

frames.label: Place
frames.narration: 1 drops into the hole. The prefix of length 2 is sorted.

arrays-and-python-costs.title: Remove the front of a list
arrays-and-python-costs.prompt: Three items sit in a contiguous array. Removing index 0 moves the other two.

frames.label: Before
frames.narration: b and c sit after a.

frames.label: Shift
frames.narration: b moves to index 0 and c moves to index 1.

frames.label: After
frames.narration: The length is 2. One removal copied n - 1 references.

dynamic-array-growth.title: Append a, b, and c
dynamic-array-growth.prompt: Capacity starts at 1 and doubles when an append finds the array full. Copied slots are marked chosen.

frames.label: Append a
frames.narration: Length 1, capacity 1. No copy.

frames.label: Append b
frames.narration: The array is full, so it doubles to 2 and copies a, then writes b.

frames.label: Append c
frames.narration: The array is full again. It doubles to 4 and copies a and b, then writes c.

recursion-and-recurrences.title: Halve 8 until 1
recursion-and-recurrences.prompt: Each call splits into two half-size calls. This frame shows one root-to-leaf path and the size at that level.

frames.label: Level 0
frames.narration: The root call holds all 8 items.

frames.label: Level 1
frames.narration: One child holds 4 items. The other child is the same size.

frames.label: Level 2
frames.narration: The next call holds 2 items.

frames.label: Level 3
frames.narration: The leaf holds 1 item. log2(8) is 3.

singly-linked-list.title: Append, then look at the tail
singly-linked-list.prompt: Head and tail both move only when the end they point at changes.

frames.label: Empty
frames.narration: Head and tail are empty. Size is 0.

frames.label: Append a
frames.narration: The only node is both head and tail.

frames.label: Append b
frames.narration: The old tail's next becomes b, and the tail pointer moves. Head stays a.

frames.label: Find index 1
frames.narration: The search starts at the head and follows one link.

stack-basics.title: Push 1, 2, 3 and pop twice
stack-basics.prompt: The right end is the top. The library Stack used here has a fixed limit.

frames.label: Push 1
frames.narration: The stack holds one item. Size is 1.

frames.label: Push 2
frames.narration: 2 is the new top. 1 stays underneath.

frames.label: Push 3
frames.narration: 3 is the top. The push order was 1, 2, 3.

frames.label: Pop, pop
frames.narration: The first pop returns 3. The second pop returns 2. 1 remains.

queue-and-deque-operations.title: Enqueue a, b, c
queue-and-deque-operations.prompt: The left end is the front. Dequeue removes from the left.

frames.label: Enqueue a
frames.narration: a is both front and back.

frames.label: Enqueue b
frames.narration: b joins the back. a stays at the front.

frames.label: Enqueue c
frames.narration: c joins the back.

frames.label: Dequeue twice
frames.narration: The first dequeue returns a. The second returns b. c remains.

comparison-sorts.title: Insertion sort [3, 1, 2]
comparison-sorts.prompt: The library insertion_sort shifts the prefix with a strict < comparison, so equal keys would not pass each other. This input has no ties.

frames.label: Start
frames.narration: The prefix of length 1 is [3].

frames.label: Insert 1
frames.narration: 1 moves in front of 3. The prefix is [1, 3].

frames.label: Insert 2
frames.narration: 2 sits between 1 and 3. The list is sorted.

merge-sort.title: Merge sort [3, 1, 4, 2]
merge-sort.prompt: Each half is sorted, then the two sorted runs are merged by taking the smaller front. Ties would take the left run, which is why the sort is stable. merge_sort returns [1, 2, 3, 4].

frames.label: Split
frames.narration: The midpoint is 2. The halves are [3, 1] and [4, 2].

frames.label: Sort halves
frames.narration: Each half of length 2 is sorted. The runs are [1, 3] and [2, 4].

frames.label: Take 1
frames.narration: Fronts are 1 and 2. Take 1.

frames.label: Take 2
frames.narration: Fronts are 3 and 2. Take 2.

frames.label: Take 3 and 4
frames.narration: 3 leaves, then 4. The merged list is sorted.

quicksort-and-partition.title: Partition [3, 1, 4, 2] with pivot 2
quicksort-and-partition.prompt: The library swaps a chosen pivot to the end, then scans. This trace starts after 2 is already at the end, which is what happens when the chosen index is the last index.

frames.label: Pivot at end
frames.narration: 2 is the pivot. The boundary starts at 0.

frames.label: See 3
frames.narration: 3 > 2, so the boundary stays 0.

frames.label: See 1
frames.narration: 1 ≤ 2. Swap it with the boundary and advance.

frames.label: Place pivot
frames.narration: 4 > 2, so it stays. Swap the pivot into index 1.

hash-chaining.title: Keys 0 and 4 share a bucket
hash-chaining.prompt: ChainingHashTable with 4 buckets stores (0, 1) and (4, 2) in the same chain, because hash(0) % 4 and hash(4) % 4 are both 0. Lookup of 0 walks that chain.

frames.label: Empty
frames.narration: Four buckets, no pairs.

frames.label: Insert 0
frames.narration: The pair (0, 1) is the only item in bucket 0.

frames.label: Insert 4
frames.narration: 4 hashes to bucket 0 and is appended.

frames.label: Lookup 0
frames.narration: The scan sees 0 first and returns 1.

binary-search-tree-operations.title: Insert 4, 2, 6, 1
binary-search-tree-operations.prompt: Each insert walks until it finds an empty child. The library inorder walk then returns [1, 2, 4, 6].

frames.label: Insert 4
frames.narration: The tree was empty. 4 becomes the root.

frames.label: Insert 2
frames.narration: 2 < 4, and the left child is empty.

frames.label: Insert 6
frames.narration: 6 > 4, and the right child is empty.

frames.label: Insert 1
frames.narration: 1 < 4 and 1 < 2. It becomes the left child of 2.

heap-operations.title: Heapify [3, 1, 4, 2]
heap-operations.prompt: Children of index i are 2i + 1 and 2i + 2. heapify sifts from the last parent down to the root. heapsort then extracts until the array is sorted ascending.

frames.label: Before
frames.narration: The array is not a heap. Index 1 holds 1, and its child at index 3 holds 2.

frames.label: Sift index 1
frames.narration: 1 is smaller than its child 2, so those values swap.

frames.label: Sift index 0
frames.narration: 3 is smaller than its child 4, so 4 becomes the root and the array is [4, 2, 3, 1].

frames.label: After heapsort
frames.narration: Repeated extraction leaves the array sorted. The library returns [1, 2, 3, 4].

graph-traversals.title: Breadth-first search from A
graph-traversals.prompt: The library breadth_first_order on this graph returns [A, B, C, D]. The queue's left end is the front.

frames.label: Start
frames.narration: A is queued and marked visited before the loop.

frames.label: Visit A
frames.narration: Dequeue A. Enqueue B and C.

frames.label: Visit B
frames.narration: Dequeue B. Enqueue D.

frames.label: Visit C and D
frames.narration: C has no new neighbor. D is last.

union-find.title: Union 0-1 and 1-2 without heuristics
union-find.prompt: Parent pointers start as self-links. The library DisjointSet without heuristics links the second root under the first.

frames.label: Singletons
frames.narration: Each item is its own parent.

frames.label: Union 0 and 1
frames.narration: find(1) is 1. Its parent becomes 0.

frames.label: Union 1 and 2
frames.narration: find(1) walks to 0. 2's parent becomes 0.

frames.label: find(2)
frames.narration: 2's parent is already 0, so the walk is one hop and 0 equals find(0).

dynamic-programming.title: Bottom-up Fibonacci through F(6)
dynamic-programming.prompt: Each cell is the sum of the two cells before it. The library keeps only the last two values. The table here shows the same numbers.

frames.label: Base
frames.narration: F(0) and F(1) are given.

frames.label: Through F(3)
frames.narration: 1 + 1 = 2, and that cell is F(3).
